title: Cellular trees with canonical predecessor maps and cardinal goodness
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, a category $\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], an arrow class $L$ in $\mathcal A$, a root $X$, and a small well-founded partially ordered set $T$. An $L$-cellular tree on $T$ with root $X$ is a functor $D:T\to X/\mathcal A$, together with, for every $t\in T$, objects $P_t,Q_t$, an arrow $c_t:P_t\to Q_t$ in $L$, an attaching arrow $a_t:P_t\to Y_{<t}$, and an arrow $b_t:Q_t\to D(t)$ such that the square with top $c_t$, left $a_t$, right $b_t$ and bottom the canonical diagram-induced arrow $Y_{<t}\to D(t)$ is a pushout. Here $Y_{<t}$ is the colimit in $X/\mathcal A$ of $D$ restricted to the inherited predecessor poset $\{s:s<t\}$. More generally $Y_E$ is the restricted colimit in $X/\mathcal A$ for a subset $E\subseteq T$, and an inclusion $E\subseteq F$ induces the canonical transition $Y_E\to Y_F$ by the colimit universal property. For an empty subset this colimit is canonically isomorphic to the identity $X\to X$. For a regular small cardinal $\kappa$, the tree is $\kappa$-good when for every $t$, both $P_t,Q_t$ are $\kappa$-presentable (their Hom functors preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits) and $|\{s:s<t\}|<\kappa$. A category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone. No presentability of the root or the diagram vertices is required.
